title: Weight Port-of-Entry: Certification Lane & Pinflow Orchestrator
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: We need an end-to-end port-of-entry for community weights that provides deterministic conversion, security checks, performance microbenchmarks, and automatic pin suggestions. This "certification lane" will be our canonical path for new open-source LLMs to flow from raw weights -> converted runtime artifact -> version pin -> published performance profile. The goal is to remove manual gates while preserving safety and predictable runtime behavior for hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Submit a community weight and observe automated pipeline that performs checksum & provenance verification, conversion to Redwood runtime artifact, quantization compatibility check, and a micro-benchmark suite.
technical_approach: Step 1: Intake service will ingest signed manifests and store original blobs in artifact-bucket. Step 2: Run deterministic conversion harness (format adapters -> canonical checkpoint -> runtime shard). Step 3: Run safety & compatibility checks (model size/parameter count, opset whitelist, license scan). Step 4: Execute quick telemetry profiles: latency microbench (1,8,512 tokens), memory/peak-GPU, and KV-cache behavior. Step 5: Generate pin recommendation metadata (semantic: model family, sharded/non-sharded, quantization candidate) and publish profile to model-catalog. Step 6: Optionally auto-pin to canary channel and trigger staged runtime smoke on dedicated pool.
rollout_plan: Phase A (internal): run against a curated list of 10 OSS models, keep results in staging catalog. Phase B (beta): enable for community uploads with manual approval step. Phase C (GA): auto-accept low-risk families and allow auto-pin for canary deployments. Rollback path: revoke pin, mark profile deprecated, and revert routing to previous model-variant.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Conversion nondeterminism causing profile mismatch. Mitigation: Add deterministic seed artifacts, require conversion hash and smoke-run consensus across two independent runners. Risk: Malicious model weights/supply chain. Mitigation: Signed manifests + provenance checks + license enforcement and quarantine policy. Risk: False positive performance regressions. Mitigation: compare against historical baseline and require N-run sampling with variance tolerances.
